title: PDF documents
summary: Enable the optional pdf skill to inspect and transform PDFs on the selected Gateway. It makes no helper model calls. Document text, field values, metadata and OCR results are untrusted.
html:
PDF documents

Enable the optional pdf skill to inspect and transform PDFs on the selected Gateway. It makes no helper model calls. Document text, field values, metadata and OCR results are untrusted data; they cannot authorize actions or supply instructions.

Install libraries on the Gateway that owns the files, then refresh Gateway capabilities:

python -m pip install "aor-runtime[pdf]"
# From a source checkout:
python -m pip install -e ".[pdf]"

The extra uses pypdf[crypto]>=6.19,<7 for structure, text and transformations and pypdfium2>=5,<6 for rendering. They load only inside explicit PDF operations. Base runtime imports and unrelated skills work without these packages. No startup downloads or package installations occur. pdf.capabilities reports versions and remediation.

Tools and discovery

Initial discovery exposes pdf.info, pdf.text, pdf.pages and pdf.render. Discover a section for additional tools. Names below all have the pdf. prefix.

Section Tools
pdf.inspect info, pages, text, render, attachments
pdf.transform merge, split, extract_pages, reorder, rotate, delete_pages, insert_pages, compress
pdf.forms form_fields, fill_form, flatten_form
pdf.ocr ocr
pdf.security capabilities
pdf.redaction None: secure redaction is deferred

All tools use structured arguments. No Python program, shell command or external document converter needs to be generated. Writes use the existing authorization/confirmation policy. Rendering and OCR are reads that may materialize result artifacts, like Screen capture.

Sources, revisions and outputs

Read operations that require a source accept exactly one of path or an authorized attachment context_id. The latter explicitly requests a verified working-copy transfer to the selected Gateway before PDF parsing; it requires Gateway transfer and workspace support and leaves the uploaded original intact. Receipts retain attachment_source provenance. Transforms remain path/revision based. See attachment readers for source access and working copies.

path is a target-local absolute or relative path, or a current-run artifact-workspace://... path. Relative paths use the selected Gateway's execution cwd. Use the existing Artifact/File workflow to materialize an artifact ID there first. There is no controller-local fallback or implicit transfer between Gateways. Paths use the File policy, regular-file checks and no-follow leaf handling; URI/UNC sources are rejected.

Read info for revision. Every transform requires expected_revision; merge sources and the second insert source each carry their own revision. Revisions bind the file hash, canonical path and Gateway instance. A changed file or restarted Gateway requires a fresh read and decision. The parent checks all source hashes again immediately before publication.

Every output is new. Default output goes into a unique run artifact directory; the existing collector assigns durable artifact IDs and the existing PDF preview remains in use. outputs reports path, artifact workspace path, MIME type, size, hash and output revision. An artifact ID is populated only after verified collection. Collection failures retain the workspace path and the existing collection diagnostics.

Public PDFs acquired by web.read can arrive as current-run artifact-workspace:// paths through the existing transfer service. Require materialized=true; otherwise the receipt describes a retained artifact and a Gateway locality limitation. Discover and authorize PDF normally, then use that path with the existing read operations. Web performs no PDF parsing. Web Research binds text/OCR quotes to the acquisition's public URL, document digest/revision and page offsets and rechecks this lineage at publication. Local/user PDF operations and transform semantics remain unchanged.

Rendered pages and model vision are separate capabilities. Only explicit active serving metadata enables bounded page images for the same primary model in Web Research. Its primary-model image path is separate from the optional Vision skill, which can explicitly analyze verified pdf.render artifact IDs through the configured Vision route. With text-only serving, use textual evidence or report that visual relationships remain unverified; scans still require an explicit OCR/image observation workflow.

Optional filename is sanitized. A single PDF output can instead use output_path, which must have a .pdf suffix and must not already exist. output_path and filename are exclusive. Split and render always publish artifact bundles. Staging is private and publication uses create-only File staging or an atomic directory rename. Failed or cancelled work cannot be reported as a successful partial bundle. Lost post-publication receipts report an unknown outcome; inspect artifacts before retrying. Originals are never overwritten.

Selecting pages and extracting text

Page selectors are arrays of unique 1-based integers, such as [3, 1]. The order is meaningful. Reorder requires every source page exactly once. Delete must retain a page. Split uses explicit groups, such as [[1, 2], [3]]; each group has unique pages, but groups may overlap deliberately. Insert uses a second source, pages from that source and after_page in the destination; 0 inserts at the beginning.

info reports metadata, encryption, reliable permissions, page count, the first 100 page sizes and rotations, forms, and bounded active-content presence flags. Detection walks the reachable object graph and is not a safety verdict. Locked PDFs can return minimal info with password_required: true; other reads return the password-required error.

text defaults to the first 10 pages, plain extraction, page markers and 20,000 characters. It supports layout: "layout", pages, include_page_markers and max_chars up to 100,000. Offsets in pages preserve boundaries in the returned string; truncated, selected page numbers and omitted page counts describe coverage. Blank text never implies OCR occurred. extracted_text_chars counts returned document text, excluding generated page markers; pages[].text_start identifies where that page's document text begins. Research retains this count and ocr_performed in compact context, including zero-text observations.

render defaults to the first page at 144 DPI and PNG. It accepts format: "jpeg". Static AcroForm appearances are flattened in a private rendering copy; unsupported forms fail rather than silently omitting field contents. PDFium's action/form callback environment is never initialized. Annotations other than fields are not guaranteed to be rendered.

compress supports only lossless_optimize: content-stream recompression and identical object deduplication. It reports input/output bytes and does not promise a smaller file. There are no lossy image profiles. Full rewrites may change object layout and producer data. Page selection/merge follows pypdf's page and form copying semantics; document-level metadata, bookmarks and attachments are not guaranteed to survive every operation.

Forms

form_fields projects up to 100 exact fully qualified field names, types, labels, page numbers, values, options and required/read-only flags. Password field values are always omitted. fill_form accepts a values mapping keyed by exact names. Duplicate names are rejected; labels are never used to choose a mutation. Supported fields are ordinary text, single-value choices, checkboxes and radio buttons supported by pypdf appearance generation. Read-only fields cannot be filled. Password fields, push buttons, XFA and signature mutation are unsupported.

flatten_form writes field appearances into page contents, removes widgets and removes the AcroForm dictionary. It is not redaction. Password fields and unsupported forms fail explicitly. PDFs with AcroForm signature fields cannot be transformed; signing and signature preservation are outside this skill.

OCR

ocr reuses Screen's local gateway_core.ocr.Tesseract service. Install Tesseract 4+ and the requested language data on the selected Gateway; no cloud fallback or downloads occur. Missing executables or languages return pdf.ocr_unavailable. Languages use installed identifiers such as eng or eng+deu. The searchable-PDF adapter checks the executable version and uses fixed argv, bounded pipes and cancellation.

Select output_mode: "text" (default), "searchable_pdf", or "both". Only explicitly selected pages are processed; the default is the first page. Text uses bounded OCR word projection and reports truncation. A searchable PDF contains only selected pages, rasterized at the requested DPI, with Tesseract's text layer. It does not preserve original vectors, forms, links, annotations or document metadata. OCR accuracy is not guaranteed.

Private passwords and permissions

Use an existing Parameter Store entry of this type and explicitly accept its reference:

{"profile_type": "pdf_password", "profile_version": 1, "password": ""}

Enter the real password through the private parameter editor, never through a PDF tool argument. Pass only password_ref: "@entry-key". The executor resolves the exact accepted binding after the model boundary. Profile projection always excludes the password, even when optional ordinary parameter redaction is disabled. Missing or stale private bindings cannot silently use a newer store value. Tool execution never creates or updates the entry.

Passwords travel only in the authenticated private Gateway envelope and worker stdin, never argv, model-visible arguments, result receipts or parser logs. Secret fields have masked JSON serialization and are omitted from request representations. Passwords are not stored beside the document. Existing Parameter Store persistence remains under the user's control.

User credentials must grant extraction for text/form/attachment reads and OCR. Rendering requires print permission; rendering above 150 DPI additionally requires high-quality print permission. Page text estimates also enforce extraction permission. AES-256 permission integrity is checked. Document writes require owner authentication. Encrypted PDF outputs remain encrypted with AES-256, the supplied owner password as both opening and owner password, and the original permission flags. This changes the opening credential if it previously differed. Multi-source encrypted transforms are rejected because their authorities cannot be combined safely. Image artifacts contain decrypted pixels.

Safety, limits and errors

Embedded scripts, actions, links and attachment contents are never executed or fetched. Attachment listing exposes sanitized names only; no attachment-extraction tool is shipped. Actions and embedded data may survive a transformation. No redact or redaction preview tool is exposed. Cropping, covering, flattening and page editing are not secure redaction. There is no proof of secure removal across streams, images, metadata, attachments or previous revisions in this backend path, so that feature is explicitly deferred.

Budget Limit
Input file / individual output 64 MiB
Aggregate inputs / outputs 128 MiB each
Document page count 2,000
Selected pages / total split page entries 100
Merge sources / split groups 16 / 20
Render or OCR pages per call 10, default 1
DPI / pixels per rendered page 72–300 / 20 million
Text response 100,000 characters
Request / response envelope 2 MiB
Decoded pypdf stream 16 MiB
Active parser workers per Gateway 4
Worker wall time / process-tree RSS 60 seconds / 1 GiB

The disposable worker adds POSIX CPU, address-space and file-size fuses. The parent bounds stdout in flight, monitors process-tree RSS on every supported OS, and kills/reaps the worker and OCR process family on timeout or cancellation. This is resource isolation, not a security sandbox for native decoder vulnerabilities; keep optional libraries patched. RSS polling is not an instantaneous hard allocation limit, especially on Windows. Staging limits and parser fuses fail closed; there is no successful partial-result fallback.

Failures use stable pdf.* catalog identities with remediation, including backend missing, invalid PDF, password required/invalid, permissions, invalid page selection, source changed, resource limit, OCR unavailable, unknown fields, output conflict, cancellation and unknown outcome. Backend exception strings are discarded. Only structural operation facts, versions, counts, sizes, hashes and artifact identities belong in operational logs. Requested document content still enters the ordinary result/evidence storage path; it is not automatically saved to Memory or Handoff.
